note: Project B preregistration, model 1.2.0, frozen through the canonical tooling. Two revisions from 1.0.0, each for a defect statable without reference to which arm it favours, each keeping the superseded run. 1.0.0->1.1.0: capability was independent of the strategic environment, so defence networks scored the same whether the US was committed or gone. 1.1.0->1.2.0: an implementation bug against the repository's own declared semantics -- Instrument.fiscal_gdp_pct is documented as a cost PER YEAR but apply_decision charged it only on increase, so a commitment once reached was held free; the result was a degenerate model whose optimum was all 21 instruments at maximum, with constant, open-loop and feedback policies scoring identically because there was nothing to choose. Under 1.2.0 the fiscal envelope binds exactly and the optimum abandons the defence budget and nuclear latency to afford the rest.

history.note: Project B preregistration. world.py, splits.py and instruments.py are hashed BEFORE scripts/qualify_world.py runs, which is the whole defence against the circularity a review identified in the first design draft ("if adaptive is no better than constant, redesign the world"). That instruction is deleted. The model and the train/dev/test seeds are fixed first, the preregistered thresholds are written down first, and whatever the gate returns is the result. Model version 1.1.0: v1.0.0 failed and tracing why exposed an independently statable realism defect -- capability was independent of the strategic environment, so defence networks scored the same whether the US was committed or gone. v1.0.0's failing numbers are kept in the record rather than discarded. Any further coefficient change requires a defect statable without reference to which arm it favours, a version bump, and a full rerun.

Project B preregistration, model 1.2.0. Two revisions from 1.0.0, each for a defect statable without reference to which arm it favours, each with the superseded run kept. 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0: capability was independent of the strategic environment, so defence networks scored the same whether the US was committed or gone. 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0: an implementation bug against this repository's own declared semantics -- Instrument.fiscal_gdp_pct is documented as a cost PER YEAR but apply_decision charged it only on increase, so a commitment once reached was held for free. The consequence was a degenerate model whose optimum was all 21 instruments at maximum and in which constant, open-loop and feedback policies scored identically because there was nothing to choose. Under 1.2.0 the fiscal envelope binds exactly and the optimum abandons the defence budget and nuclear latency to afford the rest, which is a real trade-off and an arguable position.
